text:
alex.support: Hey team — customer ACME (dedicated pool) reports intermittent 429s despite steady QPS (no big spikes). They say errors show up only when responses stream back longer than ~800 tokens.

maria.eng-sre: Can you paste sample request IDs and a short repro? streaming + long responses makes me think of token accounting + reserved pool burst window.

alex.support: They provided 3 request IDs: r_20240312_1012_a1, r_20240312_1016_b7, r_20240312_1021_c3. Customer says pattern: constant 35 RPS, single model pinned to ded-nyc-2, but 429s cluster around responses >800 tokens.

jamal.prod: Noted. Is the 35 RPS sustained or from many clients? Also which auth method? token or mTLS?

alex.support: It's a server-to-server token (api key) rotating every 6h. Traffic originates from a small fleet (3 instances). Sustained throughput.

maria.eng-sre: Sending initial telemetry request now. Looking for per-request tokenCharge, pool availableTokens, and burst-window counters.

deploy-bot: telemetry-pull successful for request r_20240312_1016_b7. Tags: customer=ACME, pool=ded-nyc-2, model=redwood-2.1-q8. tokenCharge=1420, returned_status=429.

maria.eng-sre: tokenCharge 1420 for single call explains quota exhaustion if reserved pool cap is ~1200 tokens/window. But weird because steady 35 RPS should be okay. Could be that streaming charges full token count at start of response (prefetch accounting) which subtracts from pool immediately.

tessa.cs: Customer claims their billing shows lower token totals than infra logs. They think we're double-charging for streams. Any known bug?

maria.eng-sre: No known double-charge bug. But there was a recent change to the burst allocator: it moves windowed tokens from shared to reserved pool when response latency >250ms to prioritize tail latency. That could reduce visible headroom for this customer during long streams.

jamal.prod: Do we have rollout timeline for that change? Could be coincidental with when they started seeing 429s.

maria.eng-sre: Rollout to ded-nyc completed 2024-03-05. Customer first report 2024-03-12. Correlation present. I'll check the feature flag history and canary logs.

alex.support: Customer needs temporary relief — recommended steps? Increase reserved pool cap? Or allow higher burst window?

maria.eng-sre: Short term: bump reserved-pool headroom for that account by +25% (manual override) and set fallback to compatible smaller-quantized model if pool exhausted. For longer term we'll adjust allocator to not move tokens out during long streaming responses.

tessa.cs: I'll open a support billing note explaining why infra tokenCharge spikes don't match customer-side estimate — streaming prefetch accounting can make tokens appear consumed earlier. Will add the mitigation steps we propose.

alex.support: Customer asked for repro steps we can run from their environment. Suggestion: run a steady 35 RPS load with responses set to stream and max_tokens=1200, capture request IDs.

maria.eng-sre: Agreed. Here's a quick curl load example they can run (replace $KEY and $HOST):

```bash
for i in {1..300}; do 
  curl -s -X POST https://$HOST/v1/generate 
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" 
    -H "Content-Type: application/json" 
    -d '{"model":"redwood-2.1-q8","stream":true,"input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1200}' &
  sleep 0.028
done
```

maria.eng-sre: Run for 10 minutes, then send back request IDs and time windows. We'll correlate with pool counters.

jamal.prod: I'll approve the temporary headroom increase for ACME. maria, please coordinate the override and note TTL.

maria.eng-sre: Override applied: reserved.headroom +25% for account ACME until 2024-03-20 00:00 UTC. Monitoring now.

deploy-bot: override-change applied by maria.eng-sre at 2024-03-13T15:42:10Z.

alex.support: Thanks all. I'll update ACME with repro steps, the temporary headroom, and ask them to run the curl test and return the IDs.

tessa.cs: I'll track billing inquiry and close loop once we confirm allocator fix timeline.

maria.eng-sre: Follow-ups: (1) confirm whether stream-prefetch accounting can be changed to amortize token deduction across chunks, (2) add telemetry edge-case to show "tokens reserved at start" in customer-facing console, (3) schedule allocator rollback or config tweak if multiple customers affected.

alex.support: Great. Closing thread for now, will reopen if ACME reproduces after headroom change.
